title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A bouncer over the 9-cell word 110101010 on the left; the slow right side is a list of blocks 1^(6j+1) 00, mostly sorted by length, through which waves of rewriting pass; open. Same mechanism as 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF (and probably the part03 twin).
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the first 10,000 by the kernel alone), 8 shift rules of the sweeps; the rest of the description below is observation of the run, marked as such.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,151 cells have been visited and 22,314 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.162).

claims.title: 8 shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: For every n and every tape around: A crosses 110101010 rightward writing 001111111, C crosses it leftward writing 111011101 (eight proved rules over its rotations). Each is a theorem steps (s·n) … = some … found and proved by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (F reading 1) needs 00110 or 00111 to the left; any right side starting with 1. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. F reading 1 halts. The 5-cell closed language allows that with 0011x on the left and any right window starting with 1.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tape and head as 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LE_1LC0RF_0RD--- at every one of the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the tables differ). The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 37,151 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

facts.value: bouncer with a sorted list of blocks 1^(6j+1)

sections.heading: What the machine does: bouncer with a sorted list of blocks 1^(6j+1)
html: Left of the start the tape is (110 10 10 10) repeated (tokens b a^3 with b=110, a=10), the background of a bouncer growing like √t.

Right of it, on the slow side (395 cells right of the start after 109 steps, exponent about 0.16), the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00. The settled blocks have lengths 6j + 1 and are sorted: … 1^25 0^2 1^25 0^2 1^29 0^2 1^31 0^2 … 1^31 0^2 1^35 0^2 1^37 … 1^41 0^2 1^43 … 1^47 0^2 1^49 0^2 1^49 0^2 1^9 0^2 1 0^2 1 0^2 1^59 0 1 0^2 1^5 0^2 1^11 0^2 1^2 B>0 (step 246,254,433). Blocks of length 6j + 5 (29, 35, 41, 47, 53) sit at the boundaries between groups, and the last few blocks near the right end are in the middle of being rewritten.

Over time the groups move up: near the right end the 1^25 group is gone by step 6·108 and the visible list runs from 1^31 to 1^63 at 9.5·108. It looks like a sorted counter whose digits are block lengths, incremented by 6 when a wave passes; we have not written its rule.

sections.heading: What a halt would require
html: F reading 1 halts. The 5-cell closed language allows that with 0011x on the left and any right window starting with 1.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html:
• Sweeps (lean/Sweeps.lean, kernel): A crosses 110101010 rightward writing 001111111, C crosses it leftward writing 111011101 (eight proved rules over its rotations); for every number of copies and every tape around.
  • Bounded run (lean/Blank.lean): no halt in 107 steps (native), 10,000 (kernel); the halting transition is the only way to stop.
Everything else on this page is observation of the simulated run (heuristic). Nothing here decides halting.

sections.heading: What would move it forward
html: Write the rule of one visit of the head to the right wall on the block list, check it against the run, and compare with 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF, which agrees with this machine on the first records and then diverges.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.162).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,151 cells (26,993 left of the start, 395 right), with a density of 1s of 0.601.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same run as 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LE_1LC0RF_0RD--- (observed, not proved). At every one of the first 107 steps from blank tape the two machines have the same tape and the head on the same cell. Their tables differ, and no renaming of the states turns one into the other. While they run, the states pair up as A–A, B–B, B–E, C–C, D–D, E–E, E–F, F–F (this machine first), which is not one to one. Transitions not used in these steps: this machine never uses F1 and the other never uses F1. Lean proves (lean/Twin.lean here, lock_or_break, not_halts_of_noBreak) that the two runs have the same tape, the same head position and paired states up to the first break, a configuration where the paired states act differently, and that neither machine halts if no break ever comes. A halt of either machine is itself a break, and the halting transitions of the two do not correspond, so the two are not known to halt together.

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF: 8,004,077 configurations, the last at step 8,004,076 here and step 10,000,000 there
